system.summary: Letter cipher of two-sign groups over the digits and an eleventh w-sign, with a few homophones (a, e, o, i, u) and a few unread code numbers; used in clear letters for short secret phrases.

prior_solution.where: No decipherment of Cosimo's runs (Codex 533) or of the bare 1694 passages was found on the page, in the volumes or in print (Casciu 2006, Verga 2006, DBI, Galluzzi, Kühn-Steinhausen's 1938 festivities article, NDB checked; her 1938 edition of the Electress's letters and her 1939 biography not read; Acton not read; Florence State Archive inventories and the Medici Archive Project unreachable). The key comes from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of other letters in Codex 534.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.

solution.what: Penn IIIF manifests of Codex 531, 533-537 saved; Codex 533 and 531 images fetched; every leaf of Codex 533 paged: about 35 bare cipher runs, no decipherment.

Tried the interlined Codex 531 cipher (System A, dotted 1-3 digit groups; upstream research/medici_bia names it a key-rebuild source) against Codex 533: a different system (Codex 533 uses run-on two-sign groups with an eleventh sign).
Homophonic annealers with an Italian 4-gram model tested on a synthetic text of 1,500 letters: best -4.59 per letter against -4.10 for the truth, so a keyless solve was judged unreliable.
Found System B letters in Codex 534 with the recipient's interlinear decipherment (f. 14r, 30 Oct 1690); built key v1 (20 groups) from f. 14r and froze it (sha256 8bedce85...).
Held-out test of key v1 on four interlined segments of f. 15r (39 groups): 39 of 39; 200 shuffled keys at most 28.2%. Caveat: the reader knew the key when reading the interline.
Key v2 (22 groups) from ff. 14r and 15r, frozen (sha256 64783ab8...) before the clean test.

Clean held-out test on f. 21r (5 Dec 1690): cipher transcribed from crops with the interline blanked and frozen before the interline was read; 76 of 92 covered groups match (82.6%); 200 shuffled keys at most 35.9% (mean 23.9%).

Codex 533 transcribed twice: pass A forward (agent knew the key), pass B backward by a blind agent; 704 of pass B's 811 signs agreed (pass A has 850); all 116 disagreement sites checked on full-size crops (112 settled, 4 left open); two reconciled transcriptions frozen.

Cosimo's c-with-loop is the clerks' w; w6 = i (one interline on 534 f. 396v plus 38 contexts) and 91 = u (f. 21r) added as key v3 (frozen, sha256 bdc8b174...); ww = o and 62 = q kept apart as context-only values (sha256 f5115d38...).

35 runs of Codex 533 decoded with key v3 and the context values: 318 of the 401 groups in the decode (79.3%) take a letter; 15 runs read whole, 15 in part, 5 not read; about 60% of groups read as Italian (estimate).
Bare System B passages of Codex 534 ff. 114r-116v and Codex 531 f. 4r (1694) decoded with key v2 and read at about 85-95% (estimate); code numbers open.

A second AI agent transcribed and read Codex 533 ff. 1r-1v blind from the images and froze its reading before opening the first agent's notes: same cipher words, digits confirmed, clear-text corrections ('reputatione', 'che', 'ci fanno vergogna', the instructions on 1v). It had seen a key file note naming some words.

Searched for editions or studies of the letters and the cipher, and for any 1690s report that the Electress wished to return or separate: none found in the sources opened; Acton not read; Florence State Archive and Medici Archive Project unreachable.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 825 tokens, 40 types, it-modern order 4: reading -2.592 per letter; random keys -6.86 (z 6.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.371 (mean -3.482, z 14.0); annealer on the real text -2.832. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.521; polyphony 0.016; 64 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.832

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the recipient's interlinear decipherments of the secretariat's letters in the same cipher in Montauti's papers (Codex 534 ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), frozen, tested on a held-out interlined letter, and applied to Cosimo's undeciphered autograph runs (Codex 533) and to bare passages of 1694.

credits.note: Andrew Beling, with AI agents: System B key rebuilt from the Codex 534 interlines and tested on a held-out letter; Codex 533 transcribed twice and its 116 disagreements checked on the image (112 settled); first reading of Cosimo's cipher runs and of the bare 1694 passages. Reading with a key rebuilt from a period decipherment, not an independent solution. Checked by a second AI agent of ours (1r-1v), not by a person.
Anton Francesco Montauti or his secretary: the letter-by-letter interlinear decipherments in Penn Oversize Ms. Codex 534 (ff. 14r, 15r, 21r, 396v), the source of every key pair.

texts.label: L01, Codex 533 ff. 1r-1v, undated (after June 1691; breaks off, no date line)
texts.summary: Cosimo tells Montauti that the Elector Palatine has let him know of a report, written to the Elector, that Cosimo's daughter (Anna Maria Luisa, Electress Palatine) had written asking permission to return home and separate from her husband; he says such talk shames and offends his and her reputation, speaks of 'such calumnies', and asks Montauti to act, if need be by going to Düsseldorf. A report at second or third hand that Cosimo treats as calumny; no explicit denial among the words read; the writer to the Elector is unread; undated.
texts.note: All 85 cipher groups read as words (two single-letter slips; letters on context-only values and emended digits marked in readings/letter_1r1v.md). The clear text has gaps and needs a palaeographer.

outcome.fraction_read_source: Cosimo's runs only (Codex 533, 403 groups): 40.2% of the 403 groups lie in runs read whole and 318 of the 401 groups in decode/decode_rec2_v3ctx.tsv (79.3%) take a letter value; about 60% read as Italian words is an estimate between the two (readings/runs_533.tsv). The bare 1694 passages (about 85-95% by estimate) are not included.

gaps.detail: Letters decode in part but form no word; no interline or key covers Cosimo's hand.
No interline gives them; Penn Ms. Coll. 180 Folder 114 (cipher codes 1689, 1694) not seen.

gaps.item: Codex 533 f. 26r, block of eight groups 13 14 19 25 34 39 36 37
gaps.detail: No w-sign, only 1-3-9 digits: probably another table (System A) or code numbers.

gaps.item: Clear text of Codex 533 f. 1r lines 5-6 and 11-13, f. 1v lines 1 and 3
gaps.detail: Needs a palaeographer; decides who wrote to the Elector.
Both passes' readings remain possible after the image check.

gaps.item: About 50 pages of bare System B in Codex 534 ff. 1-113
gaps.detail: Listed in bare/bare_passages.md; outside this package; readable with key v3.

outcome.notes: Montauti read Cosimo's letters at the time; the recipient's interlines in Codex 534 read the secretariat's own letters in this cipher. No decipherment of Cosimo's runs or of the bare 1694 passages was found. What is new: the reconstruction of the key from the interlines, the held-out test, the double transcription of Codex 533 and the first reading of Cosimo's cipher. ww = o and 62 = q are context-only values kept apart (key/CONTEXT_VALUES.md).
